To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@finscale.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API baseline rates + EU residency adder?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FinScale is excited about the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to pull together a short note on pricing so we can compare against our current provider. Two quick asks:

1) Can you share the baseline hosted API unit rates (prompt tokens / gen tokens / embeddings) for US-hosted service?
2) For EU customers who require data to remain in-region, what is the typical \"sovereignty\" adder (percent or fixed fee)? Do you offer a VPC/private option and how does that change pricing?

We're also evaluating a 3‑year committed volume, so if you have an anchor GTM discount or committed-volume pricing tiers that'd be useful. We'd like a high-level example invoice for ~1B tokens/month so finance and procurement can model.

Can you send the numbers and any supporting doc (rate card, residency options)?

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinScale Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procure@finscale.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API baseline rates + EU residency adder?

Hi Liam — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks.

Quick summary (high-level):
- Baseline hosted (US region): $0.0012 per prompt token, $0.0024 per generated token. Embeddings: $0.0008 per vector unit.
- EU data residency adder (hosted): default is a 22% regional premium (covers regional infra and compliance controls).
- Private/VPC deployment: one-time onboarding + infra setup fee (typical $45k) + recurring premium (we typically price Dedicated/Private at ~45–60% above baseline depending on isolation level).

We can offer committed-volume discounts that scale with sustained monthly usage; for a 3‑year commitment at ~1B tokens/month we typically move to a blended per-token rate (example below) and can apply an additional enterprise discount.

Attached: Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_Q1-2027.pdf (baseline rates + tier examples) and a short Sovereignty_Options_Summary.xlsx that compares Hosted EU, Dedicated EU, and On‑Prem options.

If it's helpful I can draft a sample invoice for the 1B token scenario (US base + EU adder variants) and loop Neha for the precise discount model.

Next steps: would you like the sample invoice based on (A) US baseline with EU hosted adder, (B) US baseline + Dedicated EU, or (C) Dedicated EU with committed discount?

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API baseline rates + EU residency adder?

Hi all — looping in the proposed commercial concession and an example blended invoice for 1B tokens/mo.

Commercial proposal (high level):
- US baseline blended (example for 1B tokens): prompt/gen blended = $0.00165/token (after standard committed-tier compression).
- EU hosted adder: base 22% -> for this opportunity we can offer a concession to 15% on the committed-tier blended rate provided FinScale signs a 36‑month commitment and agrees to quarterly usage reporting.
- Dedicated EU (tenant-isolated): onboarding fee $40k, recurring premium = +38% vs baseline blended rate. No change to SLA beyond standard enterprise unless they select the premium SLA addon.

Sample invoice (approx):
- Option A (US baseline with EU hosted adder at 15%): $0.00165 * 1B tokens * 30 days ≈ $49,500/month base -> +15% = ~$56,925/month (rounded).
- Option B (Dedicated EU): base blended $0.00165 * 1B * 30 ≈ $49,500/month -> +38% = ~$68,310/month + one-time $40k onboarding.

Notes / constraints:
- The 15% concession is time-limited and requires legal approval on standard data-processing addendum with EU SCCs.
- We cannot reduce the residency guarantee; logs/metrics for the Hosted EU option are retained in-region but we do maintain a minimal cross-border control plane for orchestration metadata (we can provide an architecture note).

Hannah — can you confirm whether FinScale needs a stronger residency promise (no control-plane cross-border) or whether the hosted-in-region + SCCs is sufficient? If they require a full no-cross-border control plane we should move them to Dedicated/Private.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API baseline rates + EU residency adder?

Liam / Eva — quick follow-up from our side with a recommended path to close.

1) Residency guarantee: for Hosted EU the operational model is that customer data (payloads, logs, metrics used for billing) are stored and processed in our EU region. A small orchestration control-plane does traverse regions for job routing; we will provide a short technical note and an extract of our SOC2 + regional audit controls. If FinScale requires absolute zero cross-border control-plane traffic we should move to Dedicated EU.

2) Concession (approved): we can offer the 15% EU adder on the committed blended rate for a 36-month term, conditional on (a) signed MSA + DPA with SCCs, (b) quarterly usage reporting, and (c) 60-day early-exit notice subject to pro-rated true-up. This is approved by me for FS-2027-045.

3) Next steps: Hannah, please deliver the sample invoices for Option A and B to Liam today; Neha please attach the short residency technical note and the NDA/Security pack. Liam/Eva — if you want a call to walk finance/legal through the residency controls we can do a 30-min slot tomorrow.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, North America Sales — Redwood Inference
